subject: Urban Planning
title: The First Zoning Law: New York 1916
description: A short lesson to help you apply The First Zoning Law: New York 1916.

hook.text: In 1916, New York City passed the first zoning law in America. The reason? A skyscraper blocked the sun.

buildup.text: The Equitable Building cast a seven-acre shadow over lower Manhattan. Neighbors lost sunlight permanently.

discovery.text: The new law created setback requirements — buildings had to step back as they rose, letting light reach the street.

twist.text: Setback rules created the iconic wedding-cake skyscrapers of New York — the Art Deco skyline was shaped by zoning law.

climax.text: Every American city adopted zoning after New York. Land use control became the most powerful tool in urban planning.

punchline.text: One building stole the sun. A law reshaped every skyline in America.

quiz.question: What building triggered New York's first zoning law?
